title: Operators and comparisons
summary: Comparing values with strict and loose equality and the relational signs, and how truthiness drives ! , && and ||.

concepts.title: Truthy, falsy and the logical operators

misconceptions.description: Believes === compares only what is written, so 7 === '7' is true.
Believes a comparison hands back one of the values it was given instead of true or false.
Believes text comparison ignores the difference between upper case and lower case.
Reads a variable or comparison at a different moment than the one asked about.
Believes == is false whenever the two sides have different types.
Believes > is true for equal values, or that >= is false for equal values.
Believes text made of digits is compared as a number.
Believes the text with more characters is always the bigger one.
Judges truthiness by what a value looks like or means, not by the rules.
Believes && and || give true or false, or always the right-hand side, instead of one operand chosen by truthiness.

conceptCard.title: Comparing with === and !==
conceptCard.body: === asks whether two values are the same. It gives true only when the value and the type both match. Two texts match only when every character matches, capitals included. !== gives the opposite answer. Both give true or false, never the values themselves.

conceptCard.title: Why == surprises: type conversion
conceptCard.body: == also compares two values, but first it converts them to a common type. So 5 == '5' is true, and false == 0 is true. This surprises many people. Use === when you want an exact match.

conceptCard.title: Greater, less and their limits
conceptCard.body: <, >, <= and >= compare two values and give true or false. > and < are false when both sides are equal; >= and <= are true then. Two texts are compared character by character, not as numbers.

lessons.title: Truthy, falsy and the logical operators

conceptCard.title: Truthy, falsy and the logical operators
conceptCard.body: In a test, every value counts as true or false. The falsy values you will meet most are false, 0, the empty text, null and undefined. Nearly every other value is truthy. ! flips a value. && and || give back one of their two operands.
